id: title:MattBro:keep the install step title on one line as events arrive

review.posthog_relevance: Changes the layout and DOM structure of the property key information display in the PostHog frontend, specifically preserving title width and allowing action chips to wrap without breaking the flex row.
review.reason: The supplied hunks demonstrate a localized, bounded change to the frontend UI. P1.F5.H1 and P1.F6.H1 show CSS class additions and a replacement of a `LemonTable` with an inline chip. This preserves the displayed information while changing the layout strategy. This is a substantive, bounded capability improvement (better layout handling) rather than a narrow maintenance or a broad,
review.uncertainty: The tier is assigned based on the visible code changes, but the actual benefit is limited to the specific UI component and does not demonstrate broader systemic risk reduction or critical path changes. No adoption or incident avoidance is inferred.

observations.limitations: All supplied hunks are from the same chunk and share a consistent, bounded change group. No PR metadata, release notes, or adoption figures are supplied, so no tier can be assigned. No tier is assigned.

observations.behavior: Adds `sm:shrink-0` to the step title's className, preventing it from shrinking on small screens.
observations.posthog_connection: Preserves the title's width alongside the live event indicator, avoiding layout shifts when an event arrives.

observations.behavior: Adds `min-w-0` to the actions container and its children, allowing them to shrink and wrap without breaking the parent flex row.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows the check indicator and live event chip to share a row without pushing the title or other elements out of bounds.

observations.behavior: Replaces a LemonTable with a custom inline chip, removing the table and its columns, while retaining the event, ping, and timestamp display.
observations.posthog_connection: Reduces DOM and layout complexity while keeping the same live event information; the chip shares a row with the title, so the title no longer re-wraps.
